survivors_flagged.one_line: Cintas deal ($155 cash + 0.772 CTAS) is in a complicated merger-arb setup. Both sides certified Second Request compliance and agreed with the FTC not to close before Dec 11, 2026. A late-Oct Semafor report (unconfirmed) says the FTC told Cintas it will sue to block. The FTC suit/vote binary is the real catalyst, but the spread has likely already repriced on the news.
Ph3 ECLIPSE-1 (tobevibart+elebsiran, HDV) topline guided Q4 2026, ECLIPSE-2/3 Q1 2027; AASLD oral Nov 8; stock up ~130% off lows near 52w high so the binary is partly priced.

Viva Aerobus/Volaris 50/50 combination (Grupo Mas Vuelos): FTC, Colombia and shareholders (Mar-26) cleared. Mexico CNA is the last gate, approval expected before YE26 (Reuters, Oct-26) likely with route/low-cost conditions. Mid-arc, since the deal has been known since Dec-25.

verified.catalyst: The FTC is expected to vote on whether to sue to block Cintas's $155 cash + 0.772 CTAS-per-share acquisition of UniFirst before the parties' agreed Dec 11, 2026 no-close date. A suit would push the deal into litigation, toward a break and the $350M reverse termination fee. No suit would mean a close at roughly $328/share.
verified.dated_milestone: Dec 11, 2026: the date the parties agreed with the FTC not to close before. The FTC vote or complaint is expected on or before it. Next check: any FTC complaint filing in Nov 2026. Last news was the Oct 27-28 Semafor report, which is unconfirmed. The FTC spokesperson said it has not voted.
verified.instrument: Long UNF / short 0.772 CTAS per share (hedged merger-arb spread). An unhedged long UNF carries CTAS beta, since about 53% of the consideration is in stock.
verified.bloom_gates: G1: named counterparties (Cintas as acquirer, the FTC as regulator). G2: concrete commitments (signed merger agreement, $350M antitrust reverse termination fee, agreed timing not to close before Dec 11). G3: a specific spread figure. Deal value is $155 + 0.772 x $224.36 = $328.2 against UNF at $256.76, a 27.8% gross spread. The gross spread is quantified, but much of the FTC risk is already in that price.
verified.edge: L-M. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base is +51%: about $170 on 2025-12-19, before Cintas's renewed approach, to $256.76 today. Remaining to favorable resolution is +27.8% ($256.76 to $328.2 deal value at CTAS $224.36). Implied deal probability is about 50-55%, using a ~$175-185 standalone break price and the $350M RTF (about $19/share, payable only if blocked under antitrust law, not on the suit alone). The spread already repriced about -10.5% on Oct 27, from $279.64 to $250.40, on the Semafor report. The market treats this as a coin flip. I have no information edge on the FTC vote, so this is a fairly priced binary, not mispricing. Remaining capture is large but symmetric (roughly +71 up vs -70 to -80 down).
verified.primary_source: Semafor via TheStandard/TIKR/Newsquawk (2026-10-27/28): FTC reportedly told Cintas it will sue; FTC spokesperson says no vote yet. FMP batch-quote 2026-11-02 (UNF $256.76, CTAS $224.36). FMP EOD history (UNF $170.16 on 2025-12-19; $279.64 on 2026-10-26 to $250.40 on 2026-10-27). Deal terms and the $350M RTF as reported in the TIKR/Finimize coverage (Oct 2026).
verified.analysis: The event is real, dated and unfired. The FTC has not voted, and the Semafor report that it told Cintas it would sue is unconfirmed. Both sides certified Second Request compliance and agreed not to close before Dec 11, 2026, so the vote or complaint should land by then. UNF fell from $279.64 to $250.40 (-10.5%) on Oct 27 and has drifted back to about $257. At $256.76 the gross spread to $328.2 is 27.8%, and the implied deal probability is about 50-55% against a $175-185 break value plus a partial RTF floor. That is roughly a fair price for a likely-but-unfiled FTC suit followed by litigation, not an unpriced edge. Gap: I could not confirm whether anything happened between Oct 30 and Nov 2 because the web search budget was exhausted. The standalone break value is an estimate from the Dec 2025 pre-approach price, not a fresh DCF. The cash deal price is contractual, so it is exempt from numerator provenance.

(a) Run-up from the pre-readout base: the 52-week low was $4.82 (about the cash floor), today $11.12, so +131%, with part of that driven by the Astellas cash and not the readout. (b) Remaining: a favorable read to about $15-17 is +35-50%, while a fail falls toward cash at about $5.5-6.0 (-45-50%). Probability-weighted EV is about $13.9, roughly +25%. The event is real and forward but about half-harvested.
verified.primary_source: Vir Q4-2025 earnings 8-K Ex-99.2 (sec.gov, 2026-02-23): ECLIPSE-1 topline Q4 2026, ECLIPSE-2/3 Q1 2027. Q2-2026 results (2026-08-05, via pulse2/marketbeat): cash about $1.01B, runway 2H-2028. FMP quote 2026-11-02: $11.12, 52w range 4.815-12.19, mcap $1.88B.
verified.analysis: The dated forward binary is real and has not fired. The company guided ECLIPSE-1 topline to Q4 2026 (Feb-2026 8-K) and all three ECLIPSE trials are fully enrolled. Cash of about $1.01B gives a runway into 2H-2028, which puts a hard floor near $5.6/sh with no preferred or debt waterfall to worry about. The trouble is that the stock sits at $11.12, 9% below its $12.19 52-week high and +131% off the lows, so the high-probability success case is largely priced. What is left is a roughly 1.6:1 skew (+40% vs -48%) on a high-P(success) binary, which is a reasonable WATCH but not an ACTIVE entry; it would upgrade on a pullback toward $8-9 before the readout. Gaps: the Nov-8 AASLD oral and any October timing update were not verified because the search budget ran out, and the Nov-2025 enrollment PR had put topline in Q1 2027, so the 11-05 call carries real slip risk to the dated milestone.

verified.catalyst: Mexico's CNA ruling on the Volaris/Viva Aerobus 50/50 combination into Grupo Mas Vuelos, the last open regulatory gate, is expected before YE26 and likely with conditions on fares, routes and slots.
verified.dated_milestone: CNA decision expected by 2026-12-31 (Reuters, six sources). FTC, Colombia and shareholder approvals were already done by Mar-26. Next dated item: CNA resolution, then the closing/share-exchange date. Neither date is set.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes (named counterparty: Viva Aerobus / Grupo Mas Vuelos). G2 partial (signed combination agreement, but it is a stock-for-stock merger of equals with no cash price). G3 fail (there is no specific unpriced figure, and the upside is only a derived synergy story).
verified.edge: L. This is not a real arb: holders roll into 50% of a combined, levered ULCC, so there is no contractual spread to capture. Run-up from the pre-announcement base ($7.95 on 2025-12-17, before the 2025-12-19 announcement jump to $9.49) to today ($6.86) is -14%. The deal pop has fully reversed and the stock sits below its undisturbed price. Remaining capture to a provenance-checked favorable-resolution value cannot be stated: there is no contractual deal value, and the cap table and lease/debt waterfall of the combined entity were not re-derived (lookup budget exhausted). An approval that Reuters already widely reported as likely is probably not a re-rating event by itself. The tail risks are conditions that bite (fare caps, slot divestitures) or a block.
verified.primary_source: Mexico News Daily citing Reuters (six sources), 'Viva-Volaris airlines merger likely to proceed', Oct-2026. mexicobusiness.news, 'US FTC Clears Volaris-Viva Merger into Grupo Mas Vuelos' (2026). DLA Piper, 'Volaris-Viva Aerobus merger', 2026-04-03. FMP quote 2026-11-02 ($6.855). FMP EOD 2025-12-17 ($7.95) / 2025-12-19 ($9.49). Volaris Q3-26 results, GlobeNewswire 2026-10-26.
verified.analysis: The event is real and forward: the CNA is the last gate, and the Reuters/Mexico News Daily report says approval is expected before YE26 with consumer-protection, route and low-cost conditions. But the event belongs to the wrong lane. It is a 50/50 all-stock combination, so approval only unlocks synergy value whose size depends on what the CNA imposes, and nothing contractual pins a price. The stock has round-tripped below its pre-deal base ($6.86 vs $7.95) on an ULCC loss cycle (Q3-26 EPS -$0.23, Zacks Rank 5 on 2026-10-16), so this is an airline-fundamentals call, not an event spread. Gap: I did not re-derive the combined-entity equity waterfall or look for a CNA ruling after October; the search budget ran out.
